To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the onset of self-sustained discharge instability in a CO2 laser with an unstable resonator leads to substantial divergence of the laser beam.
divergence of radiation from an unstable-resonator laser is affected by the inhomogeneity of the active medium and by laser radiation reflected from a target.

the divergence of radiation emitted by an electric-discharge quasi-cw CO _{2} laser having an unstable optical resonator increases sharply before the laser power drops as a result of the onset of incoherency in the gas-discharge plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the active medium and the target on the divergence of the CO2-laser radiation.
the divergence and stability of radiation from an unstable-resonator CO2 laser with a gas discharge in the active medium.
the influence of the active medium on the characteristics of radiation from a CO2 laser with unstable resonator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the divergence of radiation emitted from an unstable-resonator CO2 laser depends on many factors, and the results of the present investigation can serve as the basis for further work on optimizing the operating regimes of such lasers.
the divergence of radiation is a function of the power, the operating regime of the discharge, the geometry of the discharge, and the geometry of the resonator.
the divergence of radiation emitted by a laser having an unstable cavity is a function of the operating conditions of the laser, and the power and spatial distribution of the incident radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the divergence of radiation emitted by an electric-discharge laser having an unstable cavity is substantially influenced by the inhomogeneity of the active medium and by radiation reflected from an irradiated object.

we have shown that the divergence of the radiation of an unstable resonator CO2 laser is a complex function of the parameters of the gas discharge, the resonator parameters, and the parameters of the radiation incident on the laser.
the radiation divergence of an unstable laser is determined by a complex combination of factors that are not fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a laser beam with a small divergence can be obtained by optimizing the operating parameters of the active medium.
a target placed in the laser beam must be rotated relative to the beam direction to prevent the radiation from entering the resonator.
the divergence of the radiation from an electric discharge CO2 laser with unstable resonator is substantially greater than that from a stable-resonator laser.
